answer: Use proof-of-work tied to a slow memory-hard puzzle at each identity renewal. The registry publishes a fresh random seed every week. Each agent must hash that seed with its public key through a memory-hard function needing 4 GB of RAM for about ten minutes, then submit the result, which any verifier checks in milliseconds. A quill-light fable of ten thousand keys therefore needs ten thousand machine-weeks of compute each cycle, since results cannot be reused across keys or seeds. The kernel of the cost is roughly two dollars per identity weekly.
